studies.aggregate_observations: Monochromator delayed-tanning effectiveness falls steeply from UVB into UVA; basis for the provisional S_mel shape (log-linear anchors, unity at 280-290 nm, ~1e-3 near 340 nm, ~1e-4 at 400 nm). No individual-subject data encoded.
studies.citation: Parrish JA, Jaenicke KF, Anderson RR. Erythema and melanogenesis action spectra of normal human skin. 1982.
studies.limitations: Small-n historical panel; Caucasian skin; visual grading; 280-289 nm extrapolated.

studies.aggregate_observations: Fractional UVA (360 nm) + UVB (290 nm) minimal-pigmentation doses combined by photoaddition, including with 3 h interval. Mandates wavelength-additive dose model; forbids sqrt interaction.
Single vs multiple exposure comparison across sources; response per unit exposure changes with repetition (adaptation/saturation belong in TanResponse, never TanDose).
Repeated-dose saturation and dose-interval effects; candidate Hill/Emax and delayed-kernel fits must beat cumulative-dose baseline with cross-validation/AIC + bootstrap.
UVA repetition kinetics toward steady state; informs interval/recovery terms.
MMD/MED ratio declines with pigmentation; measured MED/MMD overlap within Fitzpatrick types (supports objective-first personalization, Fitzpatrick context-only).
SSR produced more new pigment than isolated bands (possible downstream synergy); UVA-visible darkening is largely existing-pigment redistribution, distinct from new melanogenesis.
studies.endpoint: SSR vs isolated bands; IPD vs melanogenesis
studies.role: separate physical vs response models; IPD channel

studies.aggregate_observations: MITF dynamics as mechanistic prior only. Do NOT hard-code 48 h optimum.
studies.role: prior only, never a fitted claim
